catalog_quote: [Martin & Araújo 2004, 'La langue Parkatêjê: Morphologie', page image] La plupart des racines du Parkatêjê sont monosyllabiques (kwýr "manioc", kô "eau"). Les rares exemples dissyllabiques ont l'accent placé sur la dernière syllabe (ha'hêr "mur", py'ka "terre"). Les racines peuvent se combiner avec des préfixes et des suffixes. Les préfixes sont non accentués, et ne modifient pas l'accentuation de la racine. D'autre part, les suffixes sont normalement accentués (sauf si la voyelle est réduite), et ne modifient pas non plus le patron accentuel de la racine. On obtient alors des mots contenant deux syllabes accentuées successives (küm'xê're "bacuri, un fruit régional", ka'xê're "étoile"). La collision d'accent est alors maintenue et n'entraîne pas un déplacement ou une réduction de l'accent comme ce serait le cas en anglais ou en français par exemple. ... [Quaresma 2021:70-71] Por fim, ai…

audit.recode_to: none — 'morphological' (non-strict, word domain) stands on every opened source; a recode to 'fixed final, non-strict' would be an inference about primary-vs-secondary accent in root+suffix clash that no accessible source makes.
audit.reasoning: (1) Quote check: both the deciding French paragraph (Martin & Araújo 2004, PDF p.2/printed p.296) and the supporting Quaresma 2021 pp.70-71 passage are verbatim in the held files. (2) Deciding source is a 2004 lexicography conference paper, but authored by the language's sole long-term phonological describer with a phonetician; I fetched sources her primary phonology paper Araújo 1993 (etnolinguistica.org, open), p.267, which independently states stress is predictable, root-final ('acento recai na segunda sílaba, qualquer que seja sua vogal') and retained per word in compounds — confirms the root-final anchor; silent on affixes. Damulakis 2010 (fetched sources) is silent. Searches of UFPA repository, CrossRef and etnolinguistica show no stress/prosody/instrumental study of Parkatêjê exists; the unheld fuller descriptions are Araújo 1989 (PhD, print only) and Araújo 2016 dictionary. sources.citation: Araújo, Leopoldina (1993). Fonologia e grafia da língua da comunidade Parkatêjê (Timbira). In: Lucy Seki (org.), Lingüística indígena e educação na América Latina, pp. 265-271. Campinas: Editora da Unicamp.
sources.quote: 'A intensidade é previsível em Parkatêjê: as raízes costumam ser mono ou dissilábicas, caso em que o acento recai na segunda sílaba, qualquer que seja sua vogal. Em compostos, cada palavra mantém seu esquema acentual. Assim, não há necessidade de marcar a sílaba mais forte.' Phonetic forms on the same page show final and multiple stresses: [taw'ti], [zu'zutu'ti] ~ [yu'yutu'ti] 'tucano', ['krua] ~ ['kruwa] 'flecha'. Silent on prefixes/suffixes.
sources.locator: printed p.267 (end of section 1 'Estrutura silábica'); transcriptions p.267 top
sources.note: The primary phonology statement that Quaresma 2021 quotes second-hand ('Araújo 1993:267'); now held, confirms predictable root-final stress and per-word accent retention in compounds; should replace Quaresma as the supporting citation.

sources.note: Glottolog's top-ranked grammar and the describer's fullest work; Ferreira 2003 and Damulakis 2010 cite it for syllable structure/phonology. It is the place most likely to say whether root-final or suffix accent is primary in suffixed words — the point on which our 'morphological' label (vs the fixed-final coding of sister languages Canela-Krahô and Apinajé) turns.
